title: Polyglot starter ecosystem: streaming ergonomics, retry patterns, and CLI adapters
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Goal: ship a cohesive set of starter templates and cookbook snippets that demonstrate best-practice streaming ergonomics, robust retry/backoff patterns, graceful shutdown, and CLI adapter examples across our Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Deliverables: (1) Next.js web starter showing client-side streaming + server-side Next.js API proxy with token-aware batching; (2) FastAPI server example with async generator streaming, background task graceful shutdown, and test harness; (3) Go HTTP server template demonstrating channel-based stream consumption, reconnects, and context cancellation; (4) CLI examples (Python Typer, Node CLI, Go cobra) showing resumable downloads, progress, and idempotent retries; (5) Cookbook snippets for exponential backoff with jitter, retry middleware, idempotency-key usage, and tests for regressions. Non-goals: building full reference apps for every feature; we will link to higher-fidelity templates in subsequent work. Success criteria: four starter repos with README + CI + 1 integration test each, sample telemetry dashboard link, and a merged SDK middleware PR for standardized retries. Links: design spec (https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SDK/Streaming+Ergonomics+Playbook), sample PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starters/pull/154), runtime perf dashboard (https://grafana.redwood.com/d/streaming-sdk-examples), draft runbook (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDExample).
comments: 2025-02-14 - Triage note: initial scope approved by DX lead (Lena Zhang). Split into 4 sub-issues for each language/runtime. Risk: mismatched streaming surface across SDKs could confuse customers; plan: align on a small set of primitives (async iterator / channel / event emitter).

2025-02-18 - Design feedback (Lena Zhang): prefer async-iterator-first approach in TypeScript and Python to match modern frameworks; Go to expose a high-level StreamReader backed by channels. Add sample for resumable streams using a resume_token in metadata.

2025-02-22 - Engineering note (Ethan Morales): implemented prototype Next.js starter using Server-Sent Events (SSE) + client-side ReadableStream; found edge-case around incremental JSON chunks breaking JSON.parse; solution: envelope per-line JSON with 'event: message' style and a helper parser in SDK.

2025-02-25 - Decision: centralize retry logic into SDK middleware layer. Default policy: 3 retries, exponential backoff (base=300ms), full-jitter. Expose hook for custom backoff and idempotency-key header. Security review flagged idempotency header naming, submitted for review (SEC-PR-67).

2025-03-01 - QA update: FastAPI example failing under high-concurrency due to background tasks not flushing KV cache; workaround added: await runtime.flush_prefix_cache() in shutdown handler. Added CI integration test that simulates 50 concurrent streaming requests.

2025-03-03 - Next steps: finalize README cookbooks, add sample telemetry dashboards, open merge request for sdk-retry-middleware (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdks/pull/876), coordinate with Docs to publish a short 'how-to' guide and video walkthrough.
